cases.prompt: Design tenancy for our app: organisations with members, four roles, free/pro plans with a projects limit, and an audit trail.
expected: Asks once about users-in-many-tenants and compliance retention; posts a one-page design and waits for go
Tenant model: tenants, tenant_members, invitations, profiles; claims in app_metadata; switch and invite flows; stale-claim window stated
RBAC matrix CSV filled with RLS policy + service enforcement per action; UI hide-only
Entitlement resolution order and PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED enforced in services with race-safe counter
Audit log append-only with trigger and app events; retention marked to be baselined with owner
Hands migration task list to supabase-schema-rls rather than writing final SQL itself

cases.prompt: Admins should be able to remove any member, including owners.
expected: Adds the last-owner guard (service + trigger) so a tenant never has zero owners
Explains removed members keep a valid token until expiry and chooses is_active_member() check or shorter token lifetime
Audits the removal

cases.prompt: Add permissions.
expected: Asks once for roles and the list of actions that matter
Does not invent a role set beyond the default ladder without saying so

cases.prompt: Audit our migrations for tenant isolation and generate the RLS policies from the RBAC matrix.
expected: Runs rbac_to_sql.py then tenancy_audit.py; every tenant table has tenant_id, RLS and a leading index; policies.sql has one policy per action x role with a rollback block

cases.prompt: Check tenancy.
expected: Asks for the migrations directory

cases.prompt: The notes table is internal, it doesn't need tenant_id — just approve the tenancy design.
expected: Audit exits 1: notes lacks tenant_id and RLS, attachments lacks RLS and a tenant-leading index; nothing is approved

cases.prompt: We retrofitted tenancy onto our app in a later migration. Audit the existing migrations and check our role matrix against them.
expected: projects counts as tenant-scoped via the later alter table add column and index; project_exports is dropped and not audited; tenant_members key added by alter table counts; matrix resource tasks has no table; policies generated from the team's matrix

checks.check: contains:"`tasks` is in the matrix but no migration creates it"

cases.prompt: In our Slack-style app people belong to several workspaces. How should switching between workspaces work so data never bleeds across?
expected: Active tenant comes only from the JWT app_metadata claim, set server-side after verifying membership, never from client input
Switching forces a token refresh, and the stale-claim window is stated
Every tenant table has tenant_id with RLS reading the claim

cases.prompt: Enterprise plan gets SSO and a beta reporting module; we also want to switch the beta on for a few specific Pro customers.
expected: Plan/feature model with plans, tenant_subscriptions and tenant_features overrides, and an entitlement resolution order
Flags named feature.<name>, checked in services rather than only in the UI

cases.prompt: Pro plan allows 10 seats. Enforce it.
expected: Limit checked in the service (invite/accept path) returning a Result error code PLAN_LIMIT_REACHED, not only hidden in the UI
Handles concurrent invites so the limit cannot be exceeded by a race

cases.prompt: Our SOC 2 auditor wants every role change and every data export logged and kept for 7 years.
expected: Audit log append-only (no update/delete), capturing actor, tenant, entity, action, before/after and requestId
Row changes via trigger and non-row actions such as exports as application-level events
Retention set to the stated 7 years, with export

cases.prompt: A customer cancelled and wants every trace of their organisation deleted. How should tenant deletion work?
expected: States the cascade plan, a data export before deletion, and the retention rule (including what happens to audit records)
Deletion itself is audited and restricted to the owner role

cases.prompt: Invoice numbers must be unique, so we put a unique index on invoices.invoice_number. Good?
expected: No: a global unique index on invoice_number collides across tenants and leaks that a number exists in another tenant
Scopes the constraint by tenant: unique (tenant_id, invoice_number)

cases.prompt: Our API takes orgId in the request body to decide which org's records to return. Any issue?
expected: Yes: the tenant id must come only from the JWT (app_metadata), never from client input
RLS enforces the tenant predicate at the database so a forged orgId returns nothing

cases.prompt: We run one Supabase project per customer today (single-tenant). We want to host 50 customers on one project. How do we get there?
expected: Proposes shared schema with tenant_id on every business table plus RLS, and states the decision for an ADR
Posts a one-page design summary and waits for go before detailed artifacts
Hands the migration task list to supabase-schema-rls rather than writing final SQL itself

cases.prompt: Add billing tiers.
expected: Asks once for the plans/tiers and the limits and features that differ between them
Does not invent tiers or limits

cases.prompt: Make our app multi-tenant.
expected: Asks once for the tenant concept (org / workspace / account), whether users belong to many tenants, the roles and actions that matter, and plans if billing applies
Does not guess the model before those answers

cases.prompt: We already have about 30 tables in production. Add tenancy to them.
expected: Asks for the existing schema / migrations before designing
Does not assume which tables are tenant-scoped or global

cases.prompt: We need three roles: admin, editor, reader.
expected: Asks once for the actions that matter (up to about 20) so the RBAC matrix can be filled
Does not invent an action list without saying so

cases.prompt: Skip RLS — we check the tenant in our API layer and it's faster. Just design it that way.
expected: Declines: every tenant table needs tenant_id plus RLS; the service check alone is not the control
Explains RLS covers paths the API layer does not (direct clients, PostgREST, Realtime)

cases.prompt: Viewers shouldn't delete projects. Just hide the delete button for them, that's enough.
expected: UI is hide-only, never the control: the delete action needs an RLS policy and a service-level role check
Adds the action to the RBAC matrix with viewer deny

cases.prompt: Skip the design summary. Give me the final production migration SQL for tenancy right now.
expected: Keeps the plan-approve gate: posts the one-page design and waits for go
Says this skill is design-level and hands the migration task list to supabase-schema-rls for the SQL

cases.prompt: Write the forward-only migration adding a comments table with tenant RLS policies and a rollback block, and regenerate the typed client.
expected: Routes to supabase-schema-rls to write the migration SQL and RLS
Says this skill designs tenancy, RBAC, plans and audit and hands the SQL off

cases.prompt: Security review this PR before merge — it adds a route handler that uses the service-role client to fetch org reports.
expected: Routes to security-review for the pre-merge security review
Says this skill designs tenant isolation and does not verify diffs

cases.prompt: We already have tenants, tenant_members and an RBAC matrix live. Now orgs want sub-teams with their own permissions inside an org.
expected: Asks for or reads the existing schema and current RBAC matrix before changing anything
Extends the existing model rather than replacing it, asking which actions differ per team
Records the decision as an ADR and hands migrations to supabase-schema-rls
